reading.body:
NTT's Ashburn VA7 data center publishes 36 MW of IT capacity, which is 2.2 percent of Virginia's 1,639.4 MW of disclosed data center capacity.

The facility is one of only 26 sites in Virginia that publish a megawatt figure, out of 332 mapped facilities in the state. That gap is the real finding. Disclosure is the exception, not the rule, so any statewide total built from these numbers is a floor rather than a census. The 36 MW also ranks 14th among the 26 disclosing sites, which places it in the middle of the group that reports at all.

For AI specifically, the published capacity is the only hard number here. The reading converts 36 MW at 40 kW per rack to roughly 900 racks and roughly 1,100 to 1,400 accelerators, but those are assumptions about density and configuration, not operator disclosures. The 125,000 square feet of technical space is a building fact. Whether the power is contracted, whether the grid connection can be expanded, and whether the space is reserved for AI workloads are all unpublished.

What this does not tell a reader is whether the facility matters to AI scaling. A 36 MW figure says nothing about utilization, interconnection queue position, or the generation behind it. The site sits in Ashburn, five miles from Dulles, in the state's primary data center hub, but proximity to other facilities is not evidence of available power. No certifications are published, and no announced expansion is recorded.
